What an administrator does to a runner from Admin → Runners (or `spin admin runner`), what
each action leaves behind, and how to undo it. A runner takes new workspaces only while it is
`ACTIVE`; `DRAINING`, `CORDONED` and `DEAD` all take none. A suspended workspace coming back is
the one exception: a `CORDONED` runner is still where its own workspaces' memory resumes, so a
workspace whose memory only it resumes waits for the cordon to lift rather than boot elsewhere
without that memory, and boots from its disk once it has waited as long as a start waits for a
host (30 minutes); a `DRAINING` one takes nothing back.

| Action | What happens to the runner | Its workspaces | Undo |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cordon** (`spin admin runner drain`) | `DRAINING`: connected, takes no new workspace | keep running | **Activate** |
| **Drain** (`spin admin runner drain --suspend`) | the same | each is suspended with its memory and resumes on another runner; one that cannot be suspended runs on, and is named | **Activate** |
| **Drain and leave stopped** (`--suspend --leave-stopped`) | the same | suspended, and stay stopped until their owners start them | **Activate** |
| **Activate** | `ACTIVE`: placement may choose it again | - | - |
| **Remove** (`spin admin runner remove`) | a machine of an autoscaling group is given back to its group, which terminates it | refused while a workspace's disk is only there | none: the group starts another |
| **Revoke** (`spin admin runner revoke`) | credentials deleted, stream cut, `CORDONED` | refused while any is on it, unless left on purpose | none: a new machine |

The control plane also cordons a runner itself when its disk is under pressure, and clears only
its own cordon, never one an administrator set.

Cordon or drain is what you want when a runner should stop taking work for a while. Revoke is for
a machine registered with a token that should never connect again - it is being replaced, or it
may be compromised: it cannot come back as the same runner, and **Activate does not undo it**. A
machine of an autoscaling group leaves through Remove instead: revoked, it would run on, paid
for and counted by its group, so when the installation sizes a fleet, revoke refuses it and says so. For a group's machine that may
be compromised, `spin admin runner remove --taken` cuts it off first, marks every disk whose key
it was given for re-keying (`spin admin volume rekeys`), and then gives it back.

## Nothing starts, and a runner is up

The control plane says, for every placement it could not make:

```
WRN SelectHost: no suitable host found connected_hosts=1 outcome=host_takes_no_work
```

and a waiting workspace says "the connected runners take no new workspace". Every connected
runner is cordoned or drained. List them and activate the one that should take work:

```bash
spin admin runner list
spin admin runner activate <runner-id>
```

or **Activate runner** in the runner's menu. The next placement chooses it.

## Revoking or removing a runner

A runner that holds any workspace's disk - running, stopped or failed - is refused, and the
refusal names them. Delete or move them first. For a runner that is not connected, the refusal
says to recover each one onto another runner. A revoke can leave them on purpose:

```bash
spin admin runner revoke <runner-id> --leave-workspaces
```

Each then runs again only by being recovered onto another runner, giving up what this one had not
published. A group's machine removed with `--taken` takes the same flag.

Once revoked, the control plane refuses everything the runner sends with "invalid or expired
runner token", and the runner does not stop trying. Its row stays `CORDONED` and disconnected,
and nothing placed will reach it. Bring the capacity back with a new machine, which joins as a
new runner:

- **In an autoscaling group**, Remove gives the machine back and the group starts another, which
  joins by its role.
- **Self-hosted**, boot the machine again with a new registration token (`spin admin token
  create` says where the runner's bootstrap document reads it). The runner registers again.

Replacing the machine of a runner that is wedged is [Hosts](/admin/hosts/). If the machine may
be compromised, do not reuse its disk.

## A workspace on a runner that is gone

A workspace whose runner was revoked or declared dead stops at once - in the record, since nothing
runs there any more - and a start of it says to move it. Once a live runner is up, **Move to
another runner** on the workspace's page, or:

```bash
spin workspace recover <workspace>
spin workspace recover <workspace> --accept-data-loss
```

The first changes nothing and says how much its old runner had not published; the second moves it
there, and the workspace is stopped, to be started when its owner is ready. An administrator
recovers somebody else's with `spin admin workspace recover <workspace-id> --reason <why>`. A
runner that is only restarting is waited for instead, and the workspace comes back with nothing
lost.

The control plane moves the workspaces of a silent runner itself after `rehome_after_seconds`
(300 by default; 0 moves none), when the move gives up no more than `rehome_max_unpublished_bytes`
(0 by default: none). Past that, a person decides.
